headline: Farage quits his seat and asks voters to decide

sources.title: Reform UK's Nigel Farage says he'll quit as a lawmaker and seek re-election to clear name
Why has UK Reform's Nigel Farage resigned as MP? What happens next?
Reform UK's Farage resigns as MP amid funding scandal, forcing by-election

chunks.text: Nigel Farage, the leader of Reform UK, said he would {{step down}} from his seat in Parliament. He explained that he would {{hand in}} his resignation as a lawmaker and then {{run for}} the same seat again in a by-election. Farage represents the constituency of Clacton in eastern England, which he won in 2024. He said he wanted local voters to decide his future.

verbs.wrong: To take a break from work for some time
verbs.correct: To leave an important job or position

verbs.wrong: To announce something to the public
verbs.correct: To give a document to someone in charge

verbs.wrong: To ask people to vote in an election
verbs.correct: To compete in an election for a position

chunks.text: Farage's [[announcement]] comes as a parliamentary watchdog has started to {{look into}} money he received. The Parliamentary Commissioner for Standards is [[examining]] donations that Farage did not report, including a reported 5 million pound gift from a cryptocurrency businessman based in Thailand. Reporters {{pointed out}} that British rules [[require]] members of Parliament to [[declare]] large gifts. The investigation could decide whether Farage broke Parliament's standards on money.

verbs.wrong: To ask someone questions in public
verbs.correct: To examine or investigate something carefully

verbs.wrong: To criticize someone in the news
verbs.correct: To tell someone about a fact

chunks.text: Farage said he had done nothing wrong. He told reporters, 'I have not [[broken the law]] in any way at all.' Farage did not {{own up to}} any [[wrongdoing]], and he [[made clear]] he would not {{back down}}. He decided to {{speak out}} against the process. Farage described the vote as a fight of 'people vs the establishment' and said local people should judge his actions.

verbs.wrong: To say sorry for a mistake
verbs.correct: To admit that you did something wrong

verbs.wrong: To stay silent about a problem
verbs.correct: To stop demanding something or give in

verbs.wrong: To defend yourself in a court
verbs.correct: To say publicly what you think

chunks.text: Because Farage chose to {{stand down}}, a by-election will now [[take place]] in Clacton. The Labour, Conservative, and Liberal Democrat parties {{ruled out}} putting up their own candidates for the vote. Reform UK offered to pay for the election and said it would {{carry on}} its [[campaign]]. Farage, who won Clacton in 2024, [[is expected to]] {{take on}} few strong [[rivals]] and win the seat back.

vocab.def: To leave an important job or position
ex: The chief executive decided to step down after ten years.
She will step down as leader at the end of the year.
He was asked to step down from the committee.

vocab.def: To give a document to someone in charge
ex: You must hand in your report by Friday.
The minister handed in her resignation this morning.
He handed in his homework late again.

vocab.def: To compete in an election for a position
ex: She plans to run for mayor next spring.
He decided to run for a seat in Parliament.
Several people are running for the same job.

vocab.def: To examine or investigate something carefully
ex: The police are looking into the accident.
We will look into your complaint this week.
A watchdog is looking into the missing money.

vocab.def: To tell someone about a fact
ex: She pointed out a mistake in the report.
He pointed out that the rules had changed.
The teacher pointed out the correct answer.

vocab.def: To admit that you did something wrong
ex: He finally owned up to breaking the window.
No one wanted to own up to the mistake.
She owned up to taking the money.

vocab.def: To stop demanding something or give in
ex: The company refused to back down over the pay cuts.
He would not back down, even under pressure.
In the end, the manager backed down and agreed.

vocab.def: To say publicly what you think
ex: Many workers spoke out against the new rules.
She is not afraid to speak out in public.
He spoke out about the poor conditions at the factory.

vocab.def: To leave a job or official position
ex: The captain agreed to stand down after the loss.
He will stand down as chairman next month.
She stood down so a younger leader could take over.

vocab.def: To decide something is not possible
ex: The doctors ruled out a serious illness.
The party ruled out working with its rivals.
We cannot rule out more rain tomorrow.
They carried on working despite the noise.
Please carry on with your presentation.
The team carried on training in the rain.

vocab.def: To compete or fight against someone
ex: The small team will take on the champions on Sunday.
She is ready to take on anyone in the debate.
He took on a much stronger opponent and won.
The company made an announcement about new prices.
We are waiting for an announcement from the airline.

wordDefs.def: Looking at something closely to learn the truth
ex: The doctor is examining the X-ray now.
She spent an hour examining the contract.

wordDefs.def: To need something or make it necessary
ex: Most jobs require some computer skills.
These plants require very little water.

wordDefs.def: To officially report something, such as money or gifts, to an authority
ex: You must declare any goods you bring into the country.
She had to declare the cash at the airport.
He says he has never broken the law.
They had broken the law without knowing it.

wordDefs.def: Behavior that is dishonest or against the rules
ex: The manager denied any wrongdoing.
There was no proof of wrongdoing.

wordDefs.def: Said something so that nobody could misunderstand
ex: She made clear that she would not change her mind.
He made clear he was unhappy with the service.
The meeting will take place on Friday.
Our wedding will take place in a small church.

wordDefs.def: A planned set of actions to win support
ex: The charity started a campaign to collect books.
Her campaign for class president was a lot of fun.

wordDefs.def: Is likely to, because people think it will happen
ex: The train is expected to arrive at six.
She is expected to win the prize.

wordDefs.def: People or groups who compete against each other
ex: The two brothers are friendly rivals in tennis.
Our team beat its old rivals last night.

tf.s: Nigel Farage decided to step down from his seat in Parliament.
tf.why: Farage stepped down (left his position), which is exactly what he announced.

tf.s: Farage said he would carry on in his seat instead of leaving Parliament.
tf.why: Farage stepped down (left his seat). Carry on means to continue, the opposite of what he did.

tf.s: Reform UK ruled out paying for the by-election.
tf.why: Reform UK offered to pay for the by-election. Rule out means to decide against something, which is untrue here.

tf.s: Farage owned up to wrongdoing over the donations.
tf.why: Farage did not own up to (admit) any wrongdoing. He said he had done nothing wrong.

tf.s: A parliamentary watchdog began to look into the donations Farage received.
tf.why: The watchdog looked into (started to investigate) the donations, which is happening.

tf.s: Farage said he would run for his old seat again in the by-election.
tf.why: Farage will run for (compete for) his seat again, which he announced.
